We are Stephen Kanti Mahanty and Ben Lertwachara at Harvey Mudd College. Our ENGR 155 project uses an STM32L432KC MCU and UPduino FPGA to control a suspended magnet and payload.

## Introduction

Our target is a **10 g total suspended mass**, including magnet, carrier, and object, moving between **10 and 20 mm surface gaps** below a 12 V electromagnet. We have built a printed test setup, connected two Hall sensors to an ADC read by the FPGA, and tested the electromagnet with a MOSFET and sweeping PWM. The MCU receives data over a separate SPI link; reliable acquisition and feedback integration are in progress.

The hardware webpage will graph requested and estimated gap in real time, display current and faults, accept PI gain changes, and provide Stop. This report website describes that interface; the hardware control page is served separately.

## Project Status - November 15, 2026

Since the proposal, we have drafted and iterated CAD, printed and assembled the structure, received parts, tested Hall-sensor responses through the ADC, and exercised the MOSFET power stage with a PWM sweep. MCU and FPGA bring-up code, a basic design-review presentation, block diagrams, and an updated two-sheet schematic are also prepared.

**[Read the new progress report](progress.qmd)** for the build, tests, CAD iterations, schematics, source files, and next steps. The current wiring places ADC acquisition in the FPGA. Live 16-bit SPI readout is being debugged; calibrated position sensing and closed-loop levitation remain to be demonstrated.
